newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes higher, aided by oversold ideas.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes higher, aided by oversold ideas.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter closed slightly higher, boosted by sentiment the market had become oversold after its recent slide to the lowest levels for around three years.

Dealers said hedge related selling remained fairly light, despite rapid harvest progress in Kansas, with many farmers reluctant to sell at prices which equate to less than $3.00 a bushel at many Kansas locations.
"We are probably going to chop around for a while to see whether these levels bring any demand. Basically U.S. wheat is the cheapest in the world right now," one dealer said.
He noted, however, that prices could go lower if export demand doesn't pick up.
Harvesting of wheat in Kansas was expected to remain in full flow on Thursday although there was concern that rains could slow progress Friday.

Yields have been better than most expected and there was talk the state's wheat crop could be between 390 and 400 million bushels. In June the U.S. Department of Agriculture put the crop at 363.8 million.
July closed up 1-1/4 cents at $3.32-1/4 a bushel. Other months rose 1-3/4 to four cents.
